scene.note: Tickets.java joins, cuts, measures and compares the ticket's text before it goes to the printer.

steps.note: A ticket covers some adults and some children.
The two counts are added as numbers before they meet the text.
The printer gets one line with the whole party, not two numbers glued together.
Each ticket names where the passengers are going.
The first three letters are cut out, counting positions from 0.
A capital copy of them goes on the ticket, like a luggage tag.
The boat named on the ticket is cut out of the ticket's text.
It is compared with today's boat letter by letter, not by which object holds it.
The answer is true only when the two names are the same text.
The ticket's text has a length, spaces included.
The printer's line has a fixed number of characters, and the ticket uses some of them.
What is left tells Bridie whether the ticket fits on one line.
